title: Sets and maps: a first guide
summary: Sets, maps, and their basic rules, with plain explanations, examples, and questions.
abstract: Sets specify the objects under discussion, while maps describe how one object is assigned to another. A map can send different inputs to the same output or leave some outputs unused; the squaring function does both when viewed as a map of the real numbers to themselves. Images and preimages track which objects are reached and where they came from. A map has an inverse precisely when every allowed output comes from exactly one input.
